summary:
SP ratings are the story of the week across every model: R1 sits 21-12 (64%) over the last 14 days, R2 matches at 21-12 (64%), and R3 trails slightly at 20-13 (61%) — all comfortably HOT versus season baselines near 53%. That's the signal to lean on today, and it matters because both games on this two-game slate come down to starting pitching reads. Meanwhile R1 and R4 runs are both COLD and carrying 4-game losing streaks (R1 39% last 14, R4 45% last 14) — fade the runs category hard today, and note R4's bullpen is also cold at -5.8pts. The one category running red-hot everywhere, especially R4 (70% last 14, +17.8pts over baseline), is hitting — worth weighting if either lineup projects as the stronger offensive side.

On the board, NYY @ TBR is the only true consensus — all four ratings lean TBR, with R1 showing the strongest conviction at -0.94. That aligns perfectly with portfolio trends: TBR is 42-18 (70%) when picked this season and a blistering 26-10 (72%, +22.0u) on strong plays, while NYY as a pick sits at just 51% (23-22) with strong plays actually losing money (-4.0u). Schlittler vs. Peralta also plays into the hot SP trend — with SP rated at 61-64% across the board last two weeks, lean into Tampa's rotation edge here. This is close to a max-conviction spot: hot category (SP) stacked with a strong team-when-liked leader (TBR) and full model consensus.

CHW @ CLE is murkier — R1/R2/R3 lean CLE by small margins (+0.22 to +0.27) while R4 flips to CHW at -0.25, a split that should trim bet sizing. None of today's hot/cold flags cleanly intersect this one; treat it as a lower-confidence single-unit play relative to the TBR side, which is lining up with everything the model's running hot on right now.
